union.text: Colonia Agrippina, where Clovis was installed

land.text: the kingdom of the Cologne Franks, with Cologne itself, which Clovis, king of the Salian Franks, took over in 509

successors.note: Clovis 'offered his protection to the former subjects of Sigobert and Chlodoric, and thus became their king' (Sigebert the Lame page); the page has no year for the murder, the Ripuarian Franks page dates the end of the kingdom to 509. The combined realm is the Kingdom of the Franks from 510 (see the salian-franks dossier).

capitals.name: Cologne (Colonia Agrippina)
capitals.note: the Tolbiac page has the Ripuarian Franks led by Sigebert the Lame, whose capital was Cologne; the city 'finally fell to the Ripuarian Franks in 462 AD' (History of Cologne page). The Ripuarian Franks page speaks only of 'the kingdom of Cologne'. No seat is recorded before 462.

keyframe_review.note: 22,258 km2, a band of cells across the Lower Rhine country (the Netherlands and Westphalia). The Franks page: the name 'was probably first used during the Crisis of the Third Century, although there is no clear contemporary proof of this'; the older tribes later labelled Franks include the Chamavi, Bructeri and Chattuari. No page gives a boundary or the year 238, and the Ripuarian Franks page says scholars have generally accepted since the 1950s that the name Ripuarian did not originate as a tribal name: before the Cologne kingdom this row is Cliopatria's grouping of the Rhine Franks. No infobox area exists to compare.

25,568 km2: about 4,000 km2 larger than 259, the new cells (6.0-8.5 E, 49.9-51.9 N) taken from the Roman Empire's 259 shape. The Gallic Empire page does not support a Frankish gain: Postumus 'ably protected Germania Inferior against an invasion led by the Franks in the summer of 260' and 'defeated the Frankish forces at Empel'. It does say 'lands beyond the upper Rhine and Danube had to be abandoned to the barbarians within a couple of years', naming no recipient. Left as drawn; the assignment to the Franks is Cliopatria's (ledger confidence 1).
25,386 km2, same outline as 260. 'In 261, he repelled mixed groups of Franks and Alamanni to hold the Rhine limes secure.' No change of border on the page.

25,453 km2, unchanged in outline. The Franks page records Constantius Chlorus's defeat of the Franks in the Rhine-Meuse-Scheldt delta (293-310) and Constantine's campaigns against Franks and Bructeri in 306, with a Rhine bridge at Cologne (310, History of Cologne page); no page gives a border for 283-357. Unverified: page budget.

25,699 km2 (+1% on 283). 'In the spring of 358 the Salian Franks were described under that name for the only time'; Julian attacked the Salians and Chamavi, and in 360/361 crossed the Rhine near Xanten and defeated the Chattuari. No border change on the page.

28,174 km2: adds about 5,300 km2 in the far north (6.0-7.1 E, 52.4-53.1 N), taken from no other Cliopatria polity. No page opened mentions it. Left as drawn, unverified: page budget (ledger confidence 1).
28,059 km2, within 0.5% of 367. 'In 388, Arbogast entered the Frankish frontier region personally' (Franks page); no border change.
28,283 km2, within 1% of 394; no page dates a change in 395.
28,168 km2 for 396-406, within 1% of 395. The shape ends with the year of the Rhine crossing of 31 December 406 (traditional date), when Franks tried to block Vandals and Alans (Franks page).

28,394 km2, within 1%. The Crossing page: a 'permanent breach of the Rhine frontier' with Mainz, Worms, Speyer and Strasbourg pillaged, Nijmegen and Cologne apparently left intact. No Ripuarian border change.

28,174 km2, the same area as the 367 shape. The Franks page: 'The Franks took control of the area around Trier' (407-411) and Trier was 'taken and plundered by the Franks at least three times' within a few decades; the Trier page instead dates the Frankish seizure to 459 (see the 459 keyframe). Left as drawn, the Trier cells not being in this shape.

28,441 km2: one cell (about 250 km2) near 7.8 E, 49.85 N is added from the Western Roman Empire; below any page's precision, no event written. The Trier page has the Praetorian Prefecture move from Trier to Arles 'probably in 407' and Northern Gaul under Roman control along the limes 'until 460'.

32,162 km2: about 6,100 km2 more to the west and north (4.5-7.6 E, 50.5-52.7 N), 22 of the 24 new cells from the Western Roman Empire. The Germania Inferior page says the province was 'inhabited by Romans and Ripuarian Franks in the 5th century' and 'became the core of the Frankish Kingdom', with no year for either. Left as drawn (ledger confidence 1).

32,052 km2, the 439 outline. Jordanes mentions the 'Riparii' among Aetius's auxiliaries at the Catalaunian Plains in 451; Ewig argued they were a military unit, not people from Cologne. No border change.
31,985 km2, within 0.3% of 451; no page dates a change.
31,922 km2. Unchanged for 455-458; from 459 'The Franks seized Trier from Roman administration' (Trier page), see keyframe 459.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 462 shape with Cologne, which 'finally fell to the Ripuarian Franks in 462 AD', and Trier

keyframe_review.note: 40,329 km2: about 8,850 km2 of the Eifel and Moselle country (6.1-7.7 E, 49.8-50.8 N) come from the Western Roman Empire, but the shape leaves out Cologne and Trier themselves (Cologne goes to Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks row from 462, Trier to its Kingdom of Alamannia). 'The city finally fell to the Ripuarian Franks in 462 AD.' The correction puts Cologne and Trier in the Ripuarian realm; the overlap with the other two rows is for Phase C to settle (see notes).

44,276 km2 for 469-499 in Cliopatria: adds about 4,300 km2 in the east (8.25-9.4 E, 50.5-51.1 N), from no polity (one cell each from the Saxons and Alamannia); no page opened mentions that strip (ledger confidence 1; it coincides with the start of Cliopatria's Thuringian states row, 469). Adjusted after review: the Cliopatria shape holds neither Cologne nor Trier (Cologne is in its Kingdom of the Franks row, Trier in its Kingdom of Alamannia row), so the realm would lose its capital and Trier in 469 with no loss in the ledger. The Tolbiac page, reread: 'the Ripuarian Franks, whose capital was Cologne' (496); the History of Cologne page: the city 'finally fell to the Ripuarian Franks in 462 AD'. The correction therefore keeps Cologne and Trier as in keyframe 462. Trier is my reading: the Ripuarian Franks page never names it and the Trier page says 'the Franks' seized it in 459. No infobox area exists on the Ripuarian Franks page to compare.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 469 shape with Cologne, the Ripuarian capital, and Trier

keyframe_review.note: Same outline as 469 (44,276 km2) plus Cologne and Trier, for 500-509. At Tolbiac (496) the Alemanni 'abandoned the Lower Rhine and left the Ripuarian Franks alone' and 'Clovis, who profited only a little, allowed his ally to retain the territory'; Sigebert is 'a king of the Ripuarian Franks in the area of Zülpich (Tolbiac) and Cologne' (Sigebert page); in 509 'Arriving in person Clovis assembled the citizens of Cologne' (Ripuarian Franks page, reread), so Cologne is Ripuarian to the end, although Cliopatria's shape leaves it out. Trier lies in Cliopatria's Salian 500 shape and, in the salian-franks dossier, in the northern Alamannic half that Clovis wins at Tolbiac; the overlap with the Salian realm in 500-509 is for Phase C. The shape runs to 509.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 500 shape with Cologne, the Ripuarian capital, and Trier

region.text: the Lower Rhine country of the tribes later labelled Franks (Chamavi, Bructeri, Chattuari)

ledger.note: 238: the Franks of the Lower Rhine appear (Cliopatria's start year). Page silent on 238: the Franks page says the name 'was probably first used during the Crisis of the Third Century, although there is no clear contemporary proof of this', and the Ripuarian Franks page that the name Ripuarian did not originate as a tribal name. A gap for a gap-filler. Chamavi page (reread after the review): silent on 238 and on any Ripuarian state; it says only 'In the third century Chamavi and Frisians, apparently both considered Frankish peoples, settled in the Rhine delta' and that they lived north of the Roman border between the IJssel and the Lippe or Ems. Confidence stays 1; Phase C may start the state in 462.

region.text: the cells the Ripuarian shape adds in 260, west and south of the 238 outline

ledger.note: 260: Cliopatria adds about 4,000 km2 along the middle Rhine to the Franks. Page silent on a Frankish gain: Postumus 'ably protected Germania Inferior' and 'defeated the Frankish forces at Empel'; 'lands beyond the upper Rhine and Danube had to be abandoned to the barbarians within a couple of years', naming no recipient. Counterpart is the Roman Empire row these cells leave. Postumus page (reread after the review): silent on any Frankish gain in 260; it says the Gallic army broke with Gallienus 'around the year 260' 'amid the chaos of an invasion by the Alamanni and Franks' and that Postumus probably set his capital at Cologne or Trier. Confidence stays 1.

region.text: the northern strip added in 367 (6.0-7.1 E, 52.4-53.1 N)

ledger.note: 367: Cliopatria adds about 5,300 km2 in the far north. Page silent: none of the pages opened mentions it; the cells belong to no other Cliopatria polity. Great Conspiracy page (reread after the review): 'Franks and Saxons also landed in northern Gaul' in the 367 revolt; no Frankish land gain or treaty and nothing about Frisia or north of the Rhine. Confidence stays 1.

region.text: the cells added in 439 between the Meuse and the Rhine (4.5-7.6 E, 50.5-52.7 N)

ledger.note: 439: Cliopatria adds about 6,100 km2 to the west and north. Page silent on a date: the Germania Inferior page has the province 'inhabited by Romans and Ripuarian Franks in the 5th century'; it 'became the core of the Frankish Kingdom' once 'finally abandoned', with no year. Flavius Aetius page (reread after the review): silent on 439 and on any cession of Meuse-Rhine land; it dates only Aetius's 428 war against the Salian Franks (recovering 'some territory they had occupied along the Rhine'), 431 (Tournacum and Cambriacum) and the 440s. Confidence stays 1.

region.text: Trier, seized from the Roman administration

ledger.note: 459: the Franks seize Trier. 'The Franks seized Trier from Roman administration in 459'; Northern Gaul stayed under Roman control along the limes 'until 460'. The page says Franks, not Ripuarian Franks; the Ripuarian reading is mine. The Franks page has the Franks controlling 'the area around Trier' in 407-411 and sacking it 'at least three times'. Aegidius page (reread after the review): 'The Ripuarian Franks conquered Cologne and Trier from the Romans in about 457' (tagged citation needed), 'there are no clear source which give an exact date for the Frankish takeover of Cologne and Trier'; the Liber Historiae Francorum passage it quotes has the Franks take Agrippina (Cologne) and then Trier and kill Aegidius's partisans. That page names the Ripuarians for Trier too, which supports the reading here, but dates both cities about 457; the 459 of the Trier page is kept.

462: Cologne falls to the Ripuarian Franks. 'The city finally fell to the Ripuarian Franks in 462 AD.' Cologne had been the capital of the Gallic Empire (260) and was taken by the Alemanni, not the Franks, in 355 (same page). The Aegidius page puts the fall of Cologne and Trier together 'in about 457' without an exact date; the 462 of the History of Cologne page is kept.

region.text: the Eifel and Moselle country added in 462 (6.1-7.7 E, 49.8-50.8 N)

ledger.note: 462: Cliopatria adds about 8,850 km2 of the Eifel and Moselle country to the Ripuarian shape. Page silent on the land: it dates only the fall of Cologne. Aegidius page (reread after the review): silent on the Eifel; the Moselle appears only in the Trier passage. Confidence stays 1.

region.text: the strip added in 469 (8.25-9.4 E, 50.5-51.1 N)

ledger.note: 469: Cliopatria adds about 4,300 km2 to the east. Page silent: none of the pages opened mentions it. Thuringii page (reread after the review): silent on 469 and on the Ripuarians; it has Jordanes place the Thuringi 'immediately north of the Alemanni and Suevi in about 470' and dates no Frankish gain of Thuringian land before 509. Confidence stays 1.

region.text: Zülpich (Tolbiac) and the Lower Rhine the Alemanni invaded and then abandoned

ledger.note: 496: the Alemanni invade the Lower Rhine. Sigebert asked Clovis for help after an invasion (Tolbiac page; the Clovis I page: 'In 496, the Alamanni invaded and some Salians and Ripuarians reguli (kings) defected to their side'). The page names Zülpich as the usual site of Tolbiac; the zone is a 60 km radius round Cologne.

region.text: Zülpich (Tolbiac) and the Lower Rhine the Alemanni invaded and then abandoned

ledger.note: 496: Tolbiac. 'The Alemanni abandoned the Lower Rhine and left the Ripuarian Franks alone'; 'Clovis, who profited only a little, allowed his ally to retain the territory'. The page dates the battle 496 traditionally and 506 in a revised chronology.

union.text: Colonia Agrippina, where Clovis was installed

region.text: the kingdom of the Cologne Franks, with Cologne itself

ledger.note: 509: the kingdom of Cologne ends. Chloderic and Sigobert are killed and Clovis is installed at Cologne; 'Thus the independent kingdom of the Cologne Franks was voted out of existence by the people at a single assembly in 509.' The land passes to Clovis, king of the Salian Franks (the salian-franks dossier carries the matching gain). Region repaired after review: the Cliopatria 509 shape lacks Cologne, the city where Clovis was installed, so Cologne (and Trier, as in the 500 keyframe) is added.

wars.name: Postumus's defence of the Rhine against the Franks
wars.outcome: Postumus defeats the Franks at Empel in 260 and repels mixed groups of Franks and Alamanni in 261; 'no further Germanic raids for ten years'. No Frankish gain.
wars.note: No Wikipedia article of its own; the Gallic Empire page is the source.

wars.name: Constantine's campaigns against the Franks and Bructeri
wars.outcome: Campaigns against Franks and Bructeri in Germania Inferior in 306; a bridge over the Rhine at Cologne, guarded by the castellum Divitia, in 310. No border change recorded.
wars.note: The bridge date is from the History of Cologne page ('In 310 AD, Emperor Constantine I had a bridge constructed over the Rhine').

wars.name: Julian's Frankish campaigns
wars.outcome: Julian attacks the Salians and Chamavi in 358 and crosses the Rhine near Xanten in 360/361 to defeat the Chattuari. The settlement with the Salians is in the salian-franks dossier; no Ripuarian border change.

wars.name: Arbogast's Frankish campaign
wars.outcome: 'Arbogast entered the Frankish frontier region personally'; Franks raided Bructeri and Chamavi territory around Cologne. No border change.

wars.name: Crossing of the Rhine
wars.outcome: The Vandals, Alans and Suebi cross the Rhine near Mainz on 31 December 406 (traditional date) after a war with the Franks in which the Vandal king Godegisel died; 'a permanent breach of the Rhine frontier'.
wars.note: Frigeridus gives no date or place for the Frankish battle. Cologne and Nijmegen apparently left intact.

wars.name: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
wars.outcome: Attila is defeated by the Roman-led alliance under Aetius; 'Riparii' are listed among the auxiliaries by Jordanes. No border change.
wars.note: Ewig argued the Riparii were a military unit, not people from Cologne; the Franks page has Franks on both sides.

wars.name: Frankish capture of Trier and Cologne
wars.outcome: Trier is seized by the Franks in 459 and Cologne falls to the Ripuarian Franks in 462.
wars.note: Cologne's date is from the History of Cologne page. The Trier page says 'Franks'.

wars.name: Battle of Tolbiac

zones.text: Zülpich (Tolbiac) and the Lower Rhine the Alemanni invaded and then abandoned

wars.outcome: Clovis and Sigebert the Lame defeat the Alamanni near Zülpich (Tolbiac); the Alemanni leave the Lower Rhine and Clovis lets his ally keep the territory. Sigebert is wounded in the knee.
wars.note: Traditional date 496; a revised chronology gives 506.

wars.name: Battle of Vouillé
wars.outcome: Sigobert 'supported Clovis I again, against the Visigoths at the Battle of Vouillé in the spring of 507'; Clovis wins most of Aquitaine (salian-franks dossier). No Ripuarian border change.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line anywhere in the life. The Rhine is the only named frontier; the Alemannic, Salian and Saxon edges and every Cliopatria extension (260, 367, 439, 469) are approximate.

notes:
Ripuarian Franks (eu-07-a). Nine of the nine-page budget (Ripuarian Franks, Franks, History of Cologne, Battle of Tolbiac, Gallic Empire, Trier, Sigebert the Lame, Crossing of the Rhine, Germania Inferior). None of the pages has an infobox area, so the infobox comparison was impossible; areas are Cliopatria's.

What the pages support. Only the end of the state and its last decades: Cologne falls to the Ripuarian Franks in 462 (History of Cologne), Trier is seized by 'the Franks' in 459 (Trier), Sigebert the Lame is king at Cologne and Zülpich and is wounded at Tolbiac (Tolbiac, Sigebert), the kingdom is voted out of existence in 509 (Ripuarian Franks). Before 459 the pages say nothing that dates or bounds a Ripuarian state: the Ripuarian Franks page says the name did not originate as a tribal name (scholars since the 1950s) and that Gregory of Tours gives 'the first mention of the Cologne kingdom' in the early sixth century. Cliopatria's start year 238 and all its shapes before 459 are therefore unsupported (the found event is confidence 1); a gap-filler or Phase C may prefer to start the state in 462 and label the earlier ribbon 'Franks of the Lower Rhine'. The five size changes at 260, 367, 439, 462 (the Eifel strip) and 469 are Cliopatria's and carry confidence-1 gains; the 414 and trivial 395/396/407/410 changes (under 1%) are below the pages' precision and have no event.

Cross-row conflicts for Phase C. (1) Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks row 462-509 (28,600 km2, 4.15-7.15 E, 48.9-51.5 N) holds Cologne from 462; the Ripuarian shape has zero cells in common with it and leaves Cologne out, although the pages make Cologne the Ripuarian seat. The 462 correction here puts Cologne (and Trier) in the Ripuarian realm; the owner of kingdom-of-the-franks should decide whether that row is the Ripuarian core, a Romano-Frankish remnant, or a duplicate. (2) Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alamannia row holds the Trier cells from 462 to 499; the Trier page has the Franks seize the city in 459. (3) The western-roman-empire dossier names kingdom-of-the-franks as the receiver of its 462 loss; this dossier names the Western Roman Empire as the source of Cologne and Trier. (4) The roman-empire dossier's 260 loss goes to the Alemanni (the Agri Decumates); the Ripuarian 260 strip (4,000 km2, 15 of 16 cells from the Roman 259 shape) has no matching loss there.

Disagreements between pages. The Franks page has the Franks controlling the area round Trier in 407-411 and sacking it three times within a few decades; the Trier page dates the Frankish seizure to 459 and Roman control of the limes to 460. The Franks page gives 496 for Tolbiac without comment; the Tolbiac page gives 496 traditionally and 506 in a revised chronology (the contest events are dated 496 and flagged).

Not written. No vassal or occupation events (the pages have none). No rulers: the Sigebert page gives no reign dates. No capital before 462. No month on any event (no page gives one).

Gazetteer names wanted: Zülpich (place; the Tolbiac site, written here as a 60 km radius round Cologne), the Eifel (region; the 462 strip is expressed as a Cliopatria difference), Xanten and Tongeren (places, text only).


Repairs after the review (2026-10-19). Keyframes ripuarian-franks_469 and _500 are now adjust: Cliopatria's shapes for 469-509 hold neither Cologne nor Trier, so the Cliopatria shape is unioned with both (15 km radius), as in the 462 keyframe; the 509 dissolve region and identity.successors[0].land carry Cologne and Trier too. Pages reread for this: Battle of Tolbiac ('the Ripuarian Franks, whose capital was Cologne'), Ripuarian Franks ('Arriving in person Clovis assembled the citizens of Cologne'; the page lists Cologne, Bonn, the Eifel, Zülpich, Jülich and Neuss and does not name Trier). Trier remains my reading (Trier page: 'the Franks'), and in 500-509 it overlaps the Salian realm (Cliopatria's Salian 500 shape; the northern Alamannic half in salian-franks): Phase C to settle. Thin checks (same date): the six pages the reviewer named (Chamavi, Postumus, Great Conspiracy, Flavius Aetius, Aegidius, Thuringii) were opened; none dates or bounds the strips of 238, 260, 367, 439, 462 (Eifel) or 469, so those events stay at confidence 1 and are still a gap. The Aegidius page dates the Ripuarian conquest of Cologne and Trier 'about 457' (citation needed) against 459 (Trier page) and 462 (History of Cologne page); the dossier keeps the two pages' dates. Sources are now 15 against a budget of 9: six pages were reopened for the thin checks.
